title: Role Calibration and Ladder Transparency Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview
--------
Purpose: This playbook codifies Redwood's process for calibrating role levels and communicating ladder expectations across teams. It unifies the cadence, participants, decision criteria, and communication templates used by People Ops and hiring managers to ensure fairness, transparency, and predictability for contributors.

Scope: Applies to IC and manager ladders for Engineering, Product, Design, SRE, and Developer Relations. Excludes executive-level compensation reviews (handled by Finance + Exec).

Principles
----------
- Objective alignment: Role leveling decisions should map to documented competencies and observable artifacts (projects, impact metrics, code reviews, design docs).
- Calibration over evaluation: Focus on consistent interpretation of ladders across teams rather than ranking people.
- Transparency: Provide clear rationale and an explanation of expectations to affected contributors.
- Iterative improvement: Treat calibration as a process with measurable outcomes and quarterly retrospective.

Summary of process
------------------
1) Quarterly calibration windows (Q1/Q2/Q3/Q4) with a lighter ad-hoc window for new hires within 60 days.
2) Managers prepare role-change proposals using the Role Change Form (section below).
3) Calibration committee reviews proposals and supporting evidence, applies rubric, and returns a decision within 7 business days.
4) People Ops records the outcome, updates HR systems, and provides the manager with a communication template.

Owners and responsibilities
-------------------------
- People Ops (owner): Schedule windows, maintain ladder docs, facilitate committee, ensure documentation and audit trail.
- Calibration Committee (participants): Senior ICs, cross-functional managers, and one People Ops rep. Rotating membership, minimum 5 panelists.
- Hiring Manager: Submits proposal, curates evidence, and delivers the outcome to the contributor.
- Contributor: May request re-review within the ad-hoc window (see Appeals).

Calibration committee composition (example)
-----------------------------------------
- Chair: Sr. People Ops lead (facilitator, non-voting except tie-break)
- 2x senior managers from candidate's org area (peer managers)
- 2x senior ICs from adjacent organizations
- 1x cross-functional partner (e.g., Product for Engineering hires)
- Optional observer: HRBP or Compensation analyst

Rubric (high level)
-------------------
The committee scores proposals across 4 dimensions on a 1-5 scale. Final recommended level is the mode after discussion, with justification recorded.

| Dimension | 1 (Insufficient) | 3 (Expected) | 5 (Exceptional) | Key Evidence Examples |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Impact & Scope | Limited to day-to-day tasks | Owns cross-team features | Defines org-level strategy | Release metrics, product adoption, ROI
| Technical/Role Craft | Requires mentorship | Produces high-quality work independently | Sets technical direction | PRs, architecture reviews, design docs
| Leadership & Influence | Limited to direct reports | Leads multi-team efforts | Shapes company strategy | Stakeholder testimonials, meeting outcomes
| Complexity & Autonomy | Needs close supervision | Works autonomously on complex projects | Navigates ambiguity at scale | Project plans, delivery cadence

Decision rules
--------------
- If scores across dimensions are mixed, the committee prioritizes Impact & Complexity.
- Unanimous support is not required; final decision uses simple majority. Chair casts tie-break.
- Committee documents a clear "why" for each decision (2–5 bullet rationale).

Role Change Form (template)
--------------------------
Include the following in the submission (copy-paste into the form UI):
- Candidate name / role / current level
- Proposed level and effective date
- 300–500 word summary of case for change (focus on outcomes, not opinions)
- Evidence: 3–5 artifacts (PR links, metrics dashboard, customer feedback)
- Peer manager endorsements (names + 1–2 sentence rationale)
- Any open performance improvement plans (PIPs) or active coaching notes
- Suggested communication template (private note + public update wording)

Operational timeline (example)
----------------------------
- Day 0: Manager begins packet assembly in the People Ops Role Change system.
- Day 3: Packet submitted; People Ops validates completeness.
- Day 4–10: Committee review and discussion window (synchronous 60–90 minute meeting + asynchronous votes).
- Day 11: Decision recorded; manager notified with script.
- Day 12–16: Manager meets with contributor and sends manager-to-peopleops confirmation.
- Day 20: HR systems updated (payroll, title, org chart).

Communication templates
-----------------------
Private manager script (one-on-one):
- Opening: "Thank you for your contribution to X. Today I want to share the committee's decision regarding your level."
- Decision: Root-level statement (promoted / unchanged / deferred).
- Rationale: 2–3 bullets linking work to the rubric.
- Next steps: Effective date, compensation change timeline, development plan.
- Close: Invite questions and schedule follow-up in two weeks.

Public update (optional, short)
- "Please join me in congratulating NAME for their promotion to LEVEL on DATE. They led WORK."

Appeals and re-review
---------------------
- Contributors may request a re-review within 30 days of communication by submitting missing evidence.
- Appeals are handled by an expanded committee (adds 2 independent senior members).
- Appeals should raise new evidence or material errors in the original packet; not for re-arguing taste-based judgments.

Fairness, metrics, and audit
----------------------------
People Ops will track these KPIs per quarter:
- Time-to-decision (goal: <= 14 days)
- Percentage of agreed vs. escalated decisions
- Distribution of outcomes by tenure, team, manager, and self-identified demographics (for internal audit)
- Post-change retention at 6 and 12 months

Data retention: All packets and committee notes are stored for 7 years per company policy. Compensation details remain access-controlled.

Tooling and integrations
-----------------------
- Role Change Form lives in the People Ops internal portal (link: /tools/peopleops/role-change).
- Decisions are pushed to Workday and to the Permissions/Org Chart service via an automated job (cron: daily).
- Slack workflow templates exist for manager notifications.

Runbook: What to do if a packet is incomplete
-------------------------------------------
1) People Ops flags the packet in the portal and marks "incomplete" with required items.
2) Manager notified with checklist and 48-hour SLA to complete.
3) If not completed, People Ops may: a) reschedule to next window, or b) escalate to manager's director for assistance.

Quarterly retrospective checklist
--------------------------------
- Review sample of 10% of packets for rubric consistency.
- Run a small audit on demographic distribution to check for unintended bias.
- Solicit feedback from contributors who had decisions this quarter.
- Update ladder guidance and publish changelog.

Frequently asked questions (short)
--------------------------------
Q: Can managers submit off-cycle promotions?
A: Yes, for hires, retention cases, or exceptional contributions. People Ops reviews and may convene an expedited committee.

Q: How do level expectations differ between IC and Manager tracks?
A: The ladder documents separate technical and managerial competencies; calibration compares candidates to the relevant ladder.

Q: Who can see the committee notes?
A: Notes are restricted to People Ops, the committee, and the candidate's manager. Compensation numbers are additionally access-controlled.
